title: ci(test-core): force the sliced test leg to execute, not replay
body:
Fixes #18671

Second flight on this card: the first one pinned the contradiction and named the mechanism (verdict (A), comment 5736428716). This one measures the three named repairs and implements the one the measurement picks.

## The defect, in one line

CI runs two legs of the same task in one job. The whole-package leg is `pnpm turbo run test test:repo $FILTERS ...`; the file-level slice leg is `pnpm turbo run test "--filter=$PKG" --only ... -- "--shard=$SLICE"`. `--only` drops the dependency tasks out of the run graph **and out of the task hash with them**, so the slice leg's hash carries only the package's own files plus the hand-declared `$TURBO_ROOT$` inputs. A slice that IS in the shard's affected set can therefore match a main-seeded cache entry across the very change that put it in that set. Run 34746808828 did exactly that: `Cached: 1 cached, 1 total`, `73ms >>> FULL TURBO`, replaying a log a main push run had produced ~15 minutes earlier on a commit that did not contain the PR under test — while all six shards reported success, `check-test-completeness` graded the replay OK and the shard attestation said "ran to completion".

## What changed

One line in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, plus the comment above it that carries the readings:

```
-  set -- pnpm turbo run test "--filter=$PKG" --only --concurrency=4 --summarize --log-order=stream -- "--shard=$SLICE"
+  set -- pnpm turbo run test "--filter=$PKG" --only --force --concurrency=4 --summarize --log-order=stream -- "--shard=$SLICE"
```

`turbo.json` is unchanged. Nothing else is touched.

## The measurement that picked it

Three repairs were named by the first flight, verbatim: (1) `TURBO_FORCE` on that leg; (2) make the shard a task-declared env so `--only` is not needed at all; (3) drop `--only` and pay back the closure-rebuild cost that #16395 removed.

**Does the affected task actually execute?** Measured on this tree, turbo 2.10.10, on `@objectstack/service-cache` — a package whose `test` task has the same shape (`dependsOn: ["^build"]`) and which depends on `@objectstack/spec`. Sequence: build the closure passthrough-free (as the job's own preceding step does), run the slice leg once to seed the cache, then append one line to `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, rebuild the closure, and run each variant. The mutation was proven on disk (marker count 0 to 1; blob `9051f93e...` to `4edcf771...`) and restored under a trap, verified by an empty `git diff HEAD`.

| variant | tasks | turbo's own line | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--only` + passthrough (before) | 1 | `Cached: 1 cached, 1 total` / `81ms >>> FULL TURBO` / `cache hit, replaying logs` | **NOT RUN** — defect reproduced |
| `--only --force` (this PR) | 1 | `Cached: 0 cached, 1 total` / `1.15s` / `cache bypass, force executing` | runs |
| no `--only`, passthrough kept (repair 3) | 6 | `Cached: 0 cached, 6 total` / `1m54.963s` | runs, **and rebuilds the closure** |
| no `--only`, no passthrough (repair 2's shape) | 6 | `Cached: 5 cached, 6 total` / `1.512s` | runs, closure replays |

All four rows ran the same suite; only the first one did not.

**What it costs**, re-measured today at `@objectstack/cli`'s real scale, `--dry=json` against a cache the passthrough-free closure build had just filled (59 build tasks in the plan, of which 57 execute — `@objectstack/console` and `@objectstack/refd-timer-testkit` declare no `build` script, so they appear in the plan and never run):

| plan | tasks | cache |
|---|---|---|
| `--only` + passthrough (before, and with `--force`) | 1 | 1 MISS (the test) |
| no `--only`, passthrough kept (repair 3) | 60 | **60 MISS** |
| no `--only`, no passthrough (repair 2) | 60 | 57 HIT / 3 MISS (the test + the two script-less tasks) |

So repair 3 re-executes 57 real build tasks that the job's preceding step had just made replayable. Executing that closure here measured **5m11.262s** at `--concurrency=2` on a shared container, against **60ms `>>> FULL TURBO`** for the same command when its hashes are left alone (that 60ms is the control: the closure is replayable, and only the passthrough stops it being replayed). These are shared-box seconds, not idle-box seconds; the ratio is the durable half. CI runs `--concurrency=4` on a 4-vCPU runner and the job stands against a 30-minute wall.

The slice leg's own execution cost — which repairs 1, 2 and 3 all pay, because it is the cost of actually testing — is `@objectstack/cli` at 458.15s whole-package (`scripts/test-shard-timings.json`, `measuredAt: 2026-08-24`, median across six green merge_group run summaries), sliced 1/2 across shards 5/6 and 6/6, which run in parallel. On `pull_request` and `merge_group` the shard's package set IS the affected set (`scripts/ci/select-shard-packages.sh`), so a slice is scheduled only when it is affected and a replay there is wrong by construction — this is not new CI time, it is CI time the job was skipping.

**Repair 2 is out of this PR's file surface, and that is why it is not implemented.** It needs the shard to reach vitest without a run-level passthrough. vitest 4.1.11 reads no `VITEST_SHARD` (the env vars it reads are enumerable in its dist; `shard` is not among them), so the value has to be plumbed through a vitest config file — `test: { shard: process.env.OS_TEST_SHARD }` in `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`, plus an `OS_TEST_SHARD` entry in `turbo.json`'s `test` task `env`. The dispatch's surface is `ci.yml` and `turbo.json` only, so this stops here and is reported rather than widened. Two things worth knowing if it is picked up: it is the cheapest correct shape (the closure replays, 57 HIT above) and it makes the hash honest rather than only the execution; but the sliced set is data-driven (`scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs` weights by measured duration), so a newly-sliced package without the config line would silently run its whole suite on both shards, and no gate would say so.

## What this does not fix

`--force` makes the leg execute; it does not make the hash honest. The slice leg's hash stays blind to its dependency closure, so nothing in this repo fails when a slice leg's hash stops moving for an upstream source change. The first flight proposed exactly that pin and it is deliberately out of scope here: it would red `main` on the day it lands unless it lands with a repair, and its natural home is `lint.yml`, which is held behind an open PR in another lane.

## ⛔ Merging

`.github/workflows/**` is outside the PM seat's arming channel: `auto_merge` answers **HTTP 422** there, every time. **This PR merges by a human.** That 422 is a channel fact, not a tool fault — it is not to be retried, and this PR is not to be undrafted or armed by an agent seat.

## Local verification

Gate families derived on this tree with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack .github/workflows/ci.yml turbo.json` — 46 commands. Results are in the report on the card.

No changeset: nothing published moves. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` appears in no package's `files[]`.
